metadata.name: API Design Principles & OpenAPI Validation Ruleset

rules.title: Use plural resource nouns in URIs without CRUD verbs
rules.principle: URIs identify resources (nouns), while HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) express actions. Embedding verbs like /getUsers, /createOrder, or /delete-item duplicates method semantics and fragments URL design.
rules.bad_example: POST /v1/createOrder | GET /v1/getOrderById?id=42
rules.remediation: Rename the path segment to a plural resource noun and express the action via the HTTP method.

rules.title: Use lowercase kebab-case for multi-word URI path segments
rules.principle: URL paths are case-sensitive on POSIX servers and CDN caches. Mixing camelCase, PascalCase, or underscores creates ambiguity and broken client integrations.
rules.bad_example: /v1/paymentMethods/{id} or /v1/payment_methods/{id}
rules.remediation: Convert static path segments to lowercase kebab-case while keeping path parameter identifiers consistent.

rules.title: Avoid trailing slashes in endpoint paths
rules.principle: CDNs, API gateways, and OpenAPI routers treat /v1/orders and /v1/orders/ as distinct cache keys or trigger 301 redirects that strip POST bodies in older clients.
rules.bad_example: GET /v1/orders/
rules.remediation: Remove the trailing slash from all non-root endpoint paths.

rules.title: Enforce explicit major API versioning in path or base URL
rules.principle: Breaking schema changes without an explicit major version (/v1, /v2, or a documented API-Version header) break production consumers unpredictably.
rules.bad_example: GET /orders (unversioned root path and unversioned server URL)
rules.remediation: Prefix paths with a major version like /v1/... or configure a versioned base server URL.

rules.title: GET and HEAD operations must never declare a request body
rules.principle: HTTP proxies, CDNs, browsers, and OpenAPI code generators drop or reject bodies on GET/HEAD requests because GET payload semantics are undefined.
rules.bad_example: GET /v1/orders/search with requestBody: { filter: ... }
rules.remediation: Move query filters into URL query parameters, or use POST for complex structured search payloads.

rules.title: DELETE must omit required request bodies and return 204 or 202
rules.principle: DELETE removes the target resource identified by the URI. Requiring a request body breaks standard HTTP caches and proxies, and returning 204 No Content (or 202 Accepted for async deletion) signals clean completion.
rules.bad_example: DELETE /v1/orders/{id} with required requestBody and only 200 OK
rules.remediation: Remove required requestBody from DELETE and document 204 or 202 responses.

rules.title: POST resource creation should return 201 Created or 202 Accepted
rules.principle: Returning 200 OK for newly created resources blurs creation vs. read/RPC semantics. 201 Created with a Location header tells clients the canonical URI of the created resource; 202 Accepted signals asynchronous job queuing.
rules.bad_example: POST /v1/orders -> 200 OK
rules.remediation: Define a 201 (with Location header) or 202 response on resource-creating POST operations.

rules.title: Use RFC 9457 Problem Details (application/problem+json) for 4xx/5xx errors
rules.principle: Ad-hoc error shapes ({error: '...'} vs {msg: '...'}) force clients to write brittle parsers. RFC 9457 standardizes machine-readable errors with type, title, status, detail, and instance under application/problem+json.
rules.bad_example: 400 application/json: { "error": "bad input" }
rules.remediation: Return application/problem+json on 4xx/5xx responses using a shared ProblemDetails schema.

rules.title: Every operation must document explicit client and server error responses
rules.principle: Operations that only document 200/201 hide failure modes from SDK generators, API gateways, and consumers. Every operation should explicitly declare relevant 4xx responses (e.g., 400, 401, 404, 409) or default.
rules.bad_example: responses: { "200": { "description": "OK" } }
rules.remediation: Add explicit 4xx error responses (400, 401/403, 404, 429) referencing your ProblemDetails schema.

rules.title: Collection GET endpoints must enforce pagination parameters
rules.principle: Unbounded collection endpoints cause memory exhaustion, database full-table scans, and timeouts as datasets grow. Always require bounded page sizes via limit/page_size and cursor/after/page.
rules.bad_example: GET /v1/orders returning an unbounded JSON array without limit or cursor parameters
rules.remediation: Add bounded pagination query parameters (cursor/after and limit/page_size with a maximum) and return a paginated envelope.

rules.title: Prefer cursor/keyset pagination over deep offset pagination
rules.principle: SQL OFFSET N scans and discards N rows, degrading O(N) on large tables and producing duplicate/skipped items when rows are inserted mid-scroll. Keyset cursors stay O(1) via indexed seek.
rules.bad_example: GET /v1/events?offset=50000&limit=50
rules.remediation: Replace offset/skip parameters with an opaque cursor, after, or page_token parameter.

rules.title: Support Idempotency-Key header on non-idempotent POST mutations
rules.standard_ref: IETF Idempotency-Key Draft / Stripe & Adyen Standard
rules.principle: Network timeouts on POST requests leave clients unsure whether a payment or order succeeded. Accepting an Idempotency-Key header (UUIDv4/v7) lets clients safely retry without creating duplicate side effects.
rules.bad_example: POST /v1/payments with no Idempotency-Key header parameter
rules.remediation: Add an Idempotency-Key header parameter to state-creating POST endpoints and store request fingerprints for 24h+.

rules.title: Document 429 Too Many Requests and standard RateLimit headers
rules.standard_ref: RFC 6585 §4 / IETF RateLimit Header Fields Draft
rules.principle: Clients need machine-readable backoff signals to avoid thundering herds. Declaring 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After and RateLimit-Limit / RateLimit-Remaining / RateLimit-Reset headers prevents cascading retries.
rules.bad_example: No 429 response and no Retry-After or RateLimit-* headers in OpenAPI responses
rules.good_example: 429 Too Many Requests with headers Retry-After, RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset
rules.remediation: Add a 429 response (or reusable TooManyRequests response) with Retry-After and RateLimit headers.

rules.title: Enforce HTTPS (TLS 1.2+) on all non-local server URLs
rules.principle: Serving APIs over plaintext http:// exposes bearer tokens, API keys, and PII to interception and downgrade attacks. Production server URLs in OpenAPI specs must always use https://.
rules.bad_example: servers: [{ "url": "http://api.example.com/v1" }]
rules.remediation: Change all non-localhost server URLs to https://.

rules.title: Declare security schemes and apply auth on non-public operations
rules.principle: Missing securitySchemes or forgotten operation security leaves endpoints open by default in gateway configs and misleads generated clients.
rules.bad_example: No components.securitySchemes and no global/operation security array
rules.good_example: components.securitySchemes.BearerAuth (OAuth2 / JWT) applied globally or per-operation
rules.remediation: Define components.securitySchemes and apply security globally or on each protected operation.

rules.title: Never pass API keys, tokens, or secrets in URL query parameters
rules.principle: Query parameters are logged in plaintext across reverse proxies, CDN access logs, browser history, and Referer headers. Credentials belong exclusively in the Authorization header (or secure HttpOnly cookies).
rules.bad_example: GET /v1/orders?api_key=sk_live_123&token=abc
rules.remediation: Move api_key/token/secret parameters from in: query to Authorization / securitySchemes.

rules.title: Every operation needs a unique operationId and concise summary
rules.principle: SDK generators, API portals, and LLM/MCP tool adapters rely on operationId as the deterministic function name and summary as the tool description. Missing or duplicate operationIds break code generation.
rules.bad_example: GET /v1/orders with no operationId and no summary
rules.good_example: operationId: listOrders, summary: List paginated customer orders
rules.remediation: Add a unique camelCase operationId and a concise summary to every HTTP operation.

rules.title: Include Deprecation and Sunset headers on deprecated operations
rules.principle: Marking an operation deprecated: true in OpenAPI without machine-readable Deprecation and Sunset headers hides end-of-life dates from automated runtime clients.
rules.bad_example: deprecated: true with no Sunset or Deprecation response header
rules.good_example: deprecated: true + headers Deprecation: @1767225600, Sunset: Thu, 31 Dec 2026 23:59:59 GMT
rules.remediation: Document Deprecation and Sunset response headers (and Link rel="successor-version") on deprecated endpoints.

rules.title: Provide concrete examples on request and response media types or schemas
rules.principle: Abstract types without examples leave developers and mock servers guessing formats (currency units, ID prefixes, enum casing). Realistic examples enable instant mock servers and accurate AI tool integration.
rules.bad_example: content: { "application/json": { "schema": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Order" } } } (no example)
rules.remediation: Add example or examples fields on request/response media types or component schemas.

rules.title: Prefer PATCH for partial updates and support ETag / If-Match concurrency
rules.principle: PUT requires full resource replacement and silently overwrites concurrent edits unless guarded by If-Match. Use PATCH (application/merge-patch+json) for partial updates and ETag/If-Match to prevent lost updates.
rules.bad_example: PUT /v1/orders/{id} without If-Match concurrency guard or PATCH alternative
rules.remediation: Use PATCH for partial updates and support ETag / If-Match on concurrent resource mutations.

rules.title: Constrain string lengths, array counts, and numeric bounds (OWASP API4)
rules.principle: Unbounded strings, arrays, or page limits allow attackers to trigger OOM crashes, ReDoS, or excessive DB/CPU costs with a single payload. Enforce maxLength, maxItems, and maximum in schemas.
rules.bad_example: items: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } } (no maxItems or maxLength)
rules.good_example: items: { type: "array", maxItems: 100, items: { type: "string", maxLength: 128 } }
rules.remediation: Add maxLength on input strings, maxItems on input arrays, and minimum/maximum on integer parameters.

rules.title: Use ISO 8601 (RFC 3339) UTC timestamps with format: date-time
rules.principle: Ambiguous epoch seconds vs milliseconds or local timezones cause silent scheduling and billing bugs. Timestamp properties (*_at, timestamp, createdAt) should declare type: string and format: date-time in UTC.
rules.bad_example: created_at: { type: "string" } or mixed integer seconds/millis
rules.remediation: Set type: string and format: date-time on timestamp fields and standardize on UTC Z-suffixed strings.

rules.title: Enforce object-level authorization (BOLA / IDOR) on every ID lookup
rules.principle: Authentication only proves who the caller is, not whether they own /v1/orders/{order_id}. Every handler must authorize tenant/owner scope against the database record, never trusting client-supplied user_id.
rules.bad_example: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = $1
rules.good_example: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2
rules.remediation: Scope every single-resource query by authenticated principal/tenant and return 404 or 403 consistently.

rules.title: Prefer prefixed UUIDv7 / ULID identifiers over sequential integer IDs
rules.principle: Auto-incrementing integers (/orders/1001, /orders/1002) leak business volume and invite enumeration attacks. Prefixed UUIDv7 or ULIDs (ord_01933...) remain index-friendly while preventing enumeration.
rules.bad_example: /v1/invoices/1042
rules.remediation: Generate prefixed ULID or UUIDv7 identifiers for externally exposed resource IDs.

rules.title: Sign outbound webhooks with HMAC-SHA256 and timestamp replay windows
rules.principle: Unsigned webhooks allow spoofing, and signatures without a timestamp allow replay attacks. Sign timestamp + raw payload with HMAC-SHA256, verify in constant time, and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes.
rules.bad_example: POST webhook URL with raw JSON and no signature header
rules.remediation: Sign raw webhook payloads using Standard Webhooks headers and enforce exponential backoff retries.

rules.title: Use 202 Accepted and job polling resources for slow operations
rules.principle: HTTP requests that block >15-30 seconds hit gateway, load-balancer, and mobile timeouts. Return 202 Accepted immediately with a Location or status URL pointing to an operations/jobs resource.
rules.bad_example: POST /v1/exports blocking for 90 seconds before returning 200 OK
rules.remediation: Offload slow workflows to background workers and expose a /jobs/{id} polling resource or webhook.

rules.title: Keep minor releases additive without mutating types or dropping enums
rules.principle: Adding optional response fields is backward-compatible; renaming fields, changing types (string -> int), making optional inputs required, or tightening enums breaks existing clients without a version bump.
rules.bad_example: Changing status: "in_progress" to status: "processing" in /v1
rules.good_example: Add new optional fields in /v1; introduce breaking renames only in /v2
rules.remediation: Run OpenAPI breaking-change checks in CI and reserve breaking edits for a new major version.

rules.title: Use ETag, conditional GET (If-None-Match), and explicit Cache-Control
rules.principle: Returning Cache-Control and ETag headers enables CDNs and clients to revalidate with 304 Not Modified, slashing origin CPU and bandwidth. Mark authenticated/PII responses private, no-store.
rules.bad_example: No Cache-Control header on public catalog or sensitive user profile endpoints
rules.good_example: Public catalog: Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300; Private PII: Cache-Control: no-store
rules.remediation: Set explicit Cache-Control directives and ETag support on read-heavy GET endpoints.

rules.title: Represent money in integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency
rules.principle: IEEE 754 floating-point numbers (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004) cause rounding errors in billing and ledger totals. Store and transmit money as integer minor units (cents) paired with an explicit currency code.
rules.remediation: Model monetary values as integer minor units plus a 3-letter ISO 4217 currency string.

rules.title: Propagate W3C traceparent and return X-Request-Id in every response
rules.principle: When a customer reports a 500 error, support teams need a correlation ID to locate the exact trace across microservices. Echo X-Request-Id in headers and inside RFC 9457 instance fields.
rules.bad_example: Generic 500 error with no correlation or trace identifier
rules.good_example: Response header X-Request-Id: req_01J9Z... + W3C traceparent propagation
rules.remediation: Inject a request ID middleware and return X-Request-Id on both success and error responses.

rules.title: Choose REST, GraphQL, gRPC, or SSE/Webhooks by access pattern
rules.principle: Public developer APIs & HTTP caching favor REST/OpenAPI; multi-entity UI aggregators with dynamic client fields favor GraphQL (with persisted queries & depth limits); low-latency internal microservices favor gRPC/Protobuf; live AI/event streams favor SSE or Webhooks.
rules.bad_example: Exposing raw internal gRPC or unconstrained GraphQL introspection publicly to third-party webhooks
rules.good_example: External REST (OpenAPI 3.1 + RFC 9457) + Internal gRPC + Outbound Standard Webhooks
rules.remediation: Match the API style to consumer ecosystem, latency budget, caching needs, and schema governance.

rules.title: Design deterministic, typed endpoints for AI agents and MCP tools
rules.principle: Autonomous AI agents and MCP bridges convert OpenAPI operations directly into tool schemas. Clear operationId names, bounded enums, explicit error guidance (RFC 9457 detail), and idempotent retries prevent hallucinated tool calls.
rules.bad_example: Polymorphic untyped JSON blobs with ambiguous 200 OK error payloads
rules.good_example: Strict JSON Schema properties, descriptive enums, operationId, and specific RFC 9457 error details
rules.remediation: Treat OpenAPI descriptions, enums, and error messages as first-class instructions for both humans and AI agents.

rules.title: Require info.contact, license metadata, and operation tags
rules.principle: Developer portals, SDK generators, and platform catalogs group endpoints by operation tags and route incident escalations using info.contact. Specs without ownership metadata become orphaned shadow APIs.
rules.bad_example: Operations with empty tags and missing info.contact or info.license
rules.good_example: info.contact (email + url) + non-empty tags array on every path operation
rules.remediation: Populate info.contact, info.license, and at least one domain tag on every operation.

rules.title: Set minimum and maximum bounds on numeric query and input schemas
rules.principle: Unbounded integer query parameters (such as limit=999999999) or negative quantities in request bodies allow memory spikes, integer overflows, and business-logic bypasses.
rules.bad_example: limit parameter typed as integer with no minimum or maximum
rules.remediation: Define minimum and maximum constraints on every integer and number query parameter and input field.

rules.title: Set additionalProperties: false on input object schemas
rules.standard_ref: OWASP API3:2023 (Broken Object Property Level Authorization)
rules.principle: When an API binds raw JSON request payloads directly to ORM models without rejecting unknown keys, callers can overwrite internal attributes such as role, is_admin, or balance_minor.
rules.bad_example: CreateOrderRequest object schema with open additionalProperties
rules.good_example: CreateOrderRequest with additionalProperties: false and explicit writable properties
rules.remediation: Declare additionalProperties: false on mutable request body object schemas or validate against a strict DTO.

rules.title: Declare every URI path variable as in: path and required: true
rules.principle: Undeclared {id} placeholders or path parameters missing required: true cause runtime routing failures, broken typed SDK signatures, and inconsistent gateway validation.
rules.bad_example: Path /v1/orders/{order_id} with no matching parameter or required: false
rules.good_example: Parameter { name: "order_id", in: "path", required: true, schema: { type: "string" } }
rules.remediation: Check that every {variable} token in a path template has a matching in: path parameter with required: true.

rules.title: Avoid wildcard */* and text/plain API payloads
rules.principle: Wildcard media types (*/*) or text/plain for structured API payloads bypass strict MIME parsing, break client deserialization, and weaken WAF inspection.
rules.bad_example: requestBody content keyed by */* or text/plain for JSON objects
rules.remediation: Replace */* and text/plain API payload entries with application/json or standard structured media types.

rules.title: Keep JSON property casing consistent and use PascalCase schema names
rules.standard_ref: Zalando RESTful API Guidelines #118 / Google JSON Style
rules.principle: Mixing snake_case (created_at) and camelCase (updatedAt) inside the same API forces brittle per-field deserialization aliases in every SDK and confuses AI agents.
rules.bad_example: { "order_id": "1", "createdAt": "2026-11-16T10:00:00Z" } and schema name order_dto
rules.good_example: Uniform snake_case properties across payloads + PascalCase components.schemas keys (OrderPage)
rules.remediation: Pick either snake_case or camelCase consistently for all JSON keys and name components.schemas entries in PascalCase.

rules.title: Cap batch request array sizes and document 207 Multi-Status responses
rules.principle: Unbounded bulk endpoints allow single calls to exhaust database connection pools, and binary 200/500 responses hide partial failures where 19 of 20 items succeeded.
rules.bad_example: POST /v1/orders:batch returning only 200 OK with unbounded items array
rules.good_example: POST /v1/orders:batch with maxItems: 100 and 207 Multi-Status per-item result array
rules.remediation: Enforce maxItems (typically <= 100) on batch request arrays and return 207 Multi-Status (or partial error summary) for item-level failures.

rules.title: Document outbound events using OpenAPI 3.1 top-level webhooks
rules.principle: First-class top-level webhooks entries let SDKs and integration platforms generate strongly typed webhook receivers and verification helpers alongside request schemas.
rules.bad_example: Ad-hoc prose table describing webhook payloads outside OpenAPI
rules.good_example: Top-level webhooks map with event id, type, occurred_at, api_version, and example payloads
rules.remediation: Upgrade to OpenAPI 3.1 and move outbound webhook event contracts into components.schemas and top-level webhooks.

rules.title: Enforce GraphQL query depth limits, complexity budgets, and persisted queries
rules.principle: Recursive or deeply nested GraphQL selections (user { orders { items { order { ... } } } }) enable exponential database fan-out DoS through a single 200-byte query.
rules.bad_example: Unrestricted public /graphql endpoint with introspection enabled and no depth guard
rules.good_example: Persisted operations allowlist + max depth <= 10 + query complexity budget + DataLoader batching
rules.remediation: Disable production introspection for public graphs, enable trusted persisted queries, and enforce static query depth and complexity limits.

rules.title: Reserve deleted Protobuf field numbers and propagate gRPC deadlines
rules.standard_ref: Protobuf Language Guide / Buf Lint / gRPC Deadlines
rules.principle: Reusing or renumbering Protobuf field tags silently corrupts serialized wire payloads between deployments, and RPC calls without deadlines cause cascading thread exhaustion.
rules.bad_example: Deleting field 4 and reassigning tag 4 to a new field, or calling downstream RPCs with infinite timeout
rules.good_example: reserved 4; reserved "legacy_token"; plus explicit context deadlines and google.rpc.Status errors
rules.remediation: Run buf breaking in CI, reserve deleted field numbers and names permanently, and enforce mandatory RPC deadlines.

rules.title: Use OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code + PKCE and short-lived scoped tokens
rules.principle: Long-lived bearer tokens and implicit grant flows magnify credential theft blast radius. Pair PKCE for user flows with short-lived access tokens (5-15 min), fine-grained scopes, and JWKS rotation.
rules.bad_example: 30-day non-expiring JWT or Implicit flow returning tokens in URL fragments
rules.good_example: OAuth 2.1 Auth Code + S256 PKCE, 15m JWT access token, rotating refresh tokens, /.well-known/jwks.json
rules.remediation: Adopt OAuth 2.1 best current practices: PKCE S256, short access-token TTLs, scoped claims, and kid-versioned JWKS.

rules.title: Publish deprecation windows with RFC 9745 Deprecation and RFC 8594 Sunset
rules.principle: Silent endpoint removal breaks customer production pipelines overnight. Announce deprecations 6-12 months ahead with machine-readable headers, Link migration docs, and telemetry-based outreach.
rules.bad_example: Turning off /v1/orders with one week email notice or returning unannounced 404s
rules.good_example: Deprecation: @1794873600, Sunset: Sat, 15 May 2027 00:00:00 GMT, Link: <...>; rel="deprecation", then 410 Gone
rules.remediation: Establish a documented deprecation policy combining Deprecation, Sunset, Link headers, and final 410 Gone responses.
